title: fix(layout,app-shell): drag-to-reorder works within each level of a grouped sidebar (objectui#11626)
body:
Fixes #11626

Clause-②: no

## What changes

Triage's direction on the card (`5986793209`): the grouped arm of `NavigationRenderer` gets the group-free arm's sortable path, scoped to each group, and the sidebar's order store keeps an order per group key. A move into another group stays out of scope, because which group an entry sits in is app structure, not a personal order.

- **`@object-ui/layout` `NavigationRenderer`.** With `enableReorder` on, each group's children are a sortable list with a `DndContext` of their own, and so is each run of top-level entries between two groups. No list is a drop target for another. A move is reported through the existing `onReorder(reorderedItems)`: the top-level list, with the moved group's `children` reordered and carrying their positions as `order`. A grouped menu offers no grip while `searchQuery` narrows it.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell` `useNavOrder`.** A group's order is stored under the group's `id`, beside `__root__` in `objectui-nav-order-APP`. The `id` is a spec `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`), so it holds across reloads and locales and can never be `__root__`; the label is translated, so it is not the key. The store finds the moved level by diffing the report against the tree it drew, so only that level is written, and every stored level is applied on load. A group-free app's `__root__` record is byte-identical.

The resumed review found two holes the grouped arm would have inherited from the group-free arm. Both were measured before they were fixed:

- **Authored `order`.** The renderer sorts every level by `order`, and the store applied a saved order by array position only. So on an app that authors `order`, a drag was stored and then sorted straight back. Measured in both arms on the resumed head: the store was written, and the menu was still drawn in the app's order. Now a level with a saved order carries its saved positions as `order`, and a level with no saved order is passed on untouched. The moved-group detection compares `order` as well as ids, because under authored `order` a move can land on the listed id sequence.
- **Dead tab stops.** dnd-kit's sortable `attributes` (`role="button"`, `tabIndex=0`) sat on the row wrapper while its `listeners` sat on the grip. So every row was a focusable "button" from which no key could start a drag. Measured on the resumed head: 7 of 7 row wrappers were focusable, and 0 of 7 grips. Spreading that wrapper to every grouped menu would have added one dead tab stop per entry on every stock app. The grip is now the drag activator (`setActivatorNodeRef`), with attributes and listeners together on it. Live, a keyboard reorder now works.

No export, prop, type member, callback parameter or i18n key is added. `NavigationRendererProps.enableReorder` and `onReorder` keep their types; their doc comments now state the within-level scope and what `onReorder` receives. No README or guide page describes nav reorder (searched `packages/layout`, `packages/app-shell`, `content/docs` and `docs`), so no doc drifts.

## Live: a console built from this branch, against an objectstack showcase backend

The backend is the stock showcase (`objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh`), run from an objectstack worktree detached at `ba575886`, which is 14 commits behind objectstack `main` at the time of the run. Two consoles were served from source with vite against that one backend: main `0baf86f` and this branch `beef430`. The browser was Playwright Chromium, and the page was `/apps/showcase_app/showcase_task`. The list endpoint `/api/v1/meta/app` serves every group with `expanded: false` (the spec default), so each group was opened by clicking its label before it was read.

| reading | main `0baf86f` | this branch `beef430` |
|---|---|---|
| grips, every group as served | 0 | 2 (the top-level run) |
| grips with Workspace and Data Model open | 0 | 18 (2 + 12 + 4), all `tabindex=0`; no non-grip element carries the sortable description |
| mouse drag "Settings" to the top of Workspace | no grip to drag | drawn Settings, My Work, Approvals, New Project (Wizard); stored `{"grp_workspace":["nav_settings","nav_my_work","nav_review_queue","nav_new_project_wizard"]}` |
| reload | store never written | same order drawn, same record |
| keyboard: focus the Approvals grip, Space, ArrowDown, Space | n/a | focus lands on the grip; Approvals moves down one, and the record follows |
| drag "Page Authoring" above "Capability Map" | n/a | top-level run drawn Page Authoring, Capability Map; `__root__` written beside `grp_workspace` |
| drag "My Work" onto "Projects" in Data Model | n/a | My Work stays in Workspace (it lands at the end of its own list); Data Model unchanged; no `grp_data` key |
| reload after all of the above | n/a | every stored level drawn; 0 page errors |

## Reverse verification

Each mutation went through the anchor-checked ablation tool, with a restore armed on EXIT, INT and TERM. Each restore was proven: blob equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. Every run is against the two pinned files, and the mutations ran on committed head `6eb56eb`. Later commits changed no line a mutation touched; the grip refactor in `beef430` is covered by the A4 pins, which pass at `beef430`.

| mutation | expected | observed |
|---|---|---|
| A1: the grouped sortable path off (`groupedReorder = false`) | red | 16 of 22 failed: every grouped case. The group-free and search cases stayed green |
| A2: no `order` stamping in the store | the authored-`order` cases red | 3 of 22 failed: exactly those three |
| A3: moved-group detection by ids only | the case where the move lands on the listed sequence goes red | 1 of 22 failed: exactly that case |
| A4: sortable `attributes` back on the row wrapper | the activator pins red | 2 of 22 failed: the grouped and group-free activator pins |

Two readings were taken on an earlier head:

- **The app-shell suite (`cf8b3d3`).** Between `cf8b3d3` and `beef430` only `NavigationRenderer.tsx` changed: one comment line, and the grip destructuring its handle, which changes no behaviour. `packages/app-shell` is byte-identical, and the pinned app-shell file, which drives the grip through the real sidebar, was re-run at `beef430`.
- **The app-shell lint (`e42f5d5`).** `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting, so a verdict is per file, and every app-shell file is byte-identical to `beef430`.

Not run locally, and declared to CI: `check:eager-closure`, which reads a full console production build.

## Acceptance notes

- Keys: a group's order lives under its `id`. Two groups that shared an `id` would share an order; the spec describes the `id` as unique, and this change does not police that.
- Not a finding: on `/apps/showcase_app/...` no sidebar row lights and the active group loads closed, on main as on this branch. The console's own hrefs for this app use the route segment `com.example.showcase`, so the name-segment URL is a non-canonical door. The order store is keyed by the app `name` either way.
- Comment drift, left as found: the home-arm comment in `UnifiedSidebar.tsx` says `enablePinning` and `enableReorder` "both persist under `useNavOrder`". Pins persist in the favorites store (`useNavPins`, `type: 'nav'` favorites), not in `objectui-nav-order-APP`.
- Polish, left as found: the grip sits in the row's left padding against the entry icon. These are the group-free arm's classes, unchanged.

## Resumed run

This branch resumes a run lost to a container restart. It continues from head `75c86fe`, adding commits only: no rebase, amend or force-push. The lost run's commits were reviewed as written. The direction, the per-group store, the `__root__` key, the cross-group refusal and the search switch-off were kept. Five commits were added on top: `6eb56eb` (the two holes above, with their pins), `c7a5d7b` (changeset), `cf8b3d3` (a merge of `origin/main` at `0baf86f`), `e42f5d5` (a comment the activator change had made false) and `beef430` (the grip destructures its handle, which removes three refs-during-render lint warnings the first spelling had added). Nothing the lost run measured is reused: every reading above was taken in this run.
